external_invariants: Model is ResNetForImageClassification loaded from the local assets directory only (local_files_only=True) in float32; no downloads.
All weights and activations remain FP32; torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 and torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 are False and torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest').
Seed policy: torch.manual_seed(20261020) applied in prepare, matching common.configure().

Input is the real preprocessed image fixture tensor from assets/pixels.npy (3 images, NCHW float32), selected as images[torch.arange(batch) % len(images)].contiguous(); for the frozen 'online' workload batch=1, i.e. the first image, unchanged every repeat.
The model is in eval() mode and the forward pass runs under torch.inference_mode(), identical to the source infer() helper calling model(pixel_values=pixels).logits.
Batch size is fixed at 1 for this workload; the workload, data, precision and output requirements are not altered to improve the score.
Correctness requires all logits within atol=1e-4 / rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1 argmax equality against the reference; observations include every logit and the predicted class integer.

Latency is wall time around run() with CUDA synchronization at both boundaries, per the source's per-repeat timing; throughput is derived from the unchanged work amount (batch=1) and the measured elapsed time.
The adapter does not initialize CUDA or load the model at import time and never destroys the process group in reset.

selection.rationale: Repair of the concrete failure in the previous selection: that selection (execution_plan over 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb + 6870b4a6e1536342a2ef) can no longer be reused because its second group, the root model-forward group 6870b4a6e1536342a2ef (call 80ff8693d7ac3cf2433b10f2), is absent_or_unassociated in the current discovery (previous-feedback.txt resources.groups, after_status), and the current eligible groups are only the five in inputs/groups.json; a verbatim resubmission would reference a nonexistent group. The revision anchors the boundary in what the accepted plan actually left observable. State of the project: the previous trial-3c7742e65e (whole-forward CUDA Graph capture/replay installed at project.invoke) was accepted with independently measured objective 0.759316 ms vs reference 1.531324 (paired gains 0.920273/0.623743 exceeded noise bounds 0.036356/0.030822; quality pass, max_abs_error 0.0 over 1001 elements x 2 continuous steps; required-call coverage clean), so the current starting point is the accepted ~0.75-0.76 ms revision, not the 1.630656 ms original baseline; the 3.846981 ms profiled wall is hook-perturbed and is not timing evidence, and there is no communication on this single device. Current diagnostic evidence (call-resources.json for 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0): 714.341 us of CUDA across 81 kernels, all with graph id 2 and root-only association, i.e. the workload is now kernel-bound inside the replayed graph and only ~38 us of wall-kernel gap (copy_ dispatch, graph launch, clone dispatch, sync boundaries) remains outside it. Kernel composition of that 714.3 us: 347.0 us scudnn winograd 3x3 convs; 228.7 us implicit_convolve_sgemm of which the stem 7x7 stride-2 conv alone is 115.175 us on a pathological grid of 2x16x1 blocks of 8x8x1 threads (2048 threads total on a GPU with far more SMs); 56.1 us of generateWinogradTilesKernel that re-transform the constant FP32 filter weights on every replay (per-call-resources each listed with invocations 1 inside graph id 2, so they re-execute each replay although weights never change); 42.7 us over 20 bn_fw_inf_1C11 kernels that apply a fixed eval-mode affine; 39.8 us pools/elementwise/gemv/reduce. Because the accepted plan collapsed the eager op tree, no per-op groups exist anymore (index.json shows only the project family plus profiler/copy_/clone wrappers), so the only coherent editable boundary for any further change to what is captured and replayed is the whole-run execution plan itself. Groups selected: 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb (project.invoke, call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0) owns the plan that captures and replays all 81 kernels; 687b976c828d764c1ab8 (aten::copy_, call 8b4ffbf54af1c1a252b359b6, the per-run 1x3x224x224 FP32 static-input copy the plan dispatches, site child of project.invoke) and 25f0b0f6ce52aabeb54e (aten::clone, call ff665ce97a6a868dae8ae228, the per-run 1x1000 logits clone) are the two remaining dispatches the plan executes each invocation; these three edits need one another (recapture changes the copied input source and the cloned output buffer), so they are one joint execution_plan candidate. The two profiler record_function wrapper groups (d9e5d004d6d24251774f, 798df708d05932b17f71) are discovery instrumentation that brackets the replaced invocation with no parent in calls.json; they are not editable project code and are left unselected, but their calls are listed in affected_calls because the replaced region sits between them. Per-group attribution for the prior inner op families is joint_only/absent after plan install; unmeasured does not mean unoptimizable, but under the accepted plan those ops are reachable only through this plan boundary, which is where the revision is proposed. Invariants preserved: FP32 weights and activations, TF32 off for matmul and cudnn, cudnn.benchmark stays False, seed, eval()+inference_mode, frozen batch=1 fixture input, local-assets model; no workload, precision or operator-policy change is proposed.
selection.hypothesis: Replacing the accepted replay plan with a revised whole-forward capture at the same project.invoke boundary reduces latency_ms below the accepted ~0.759 ms by attacking the now-dominant replayed-GPU share (714.3 of ~752 us) plus the residual dispatch overhead, as follows, each element validated once at untimed capture time against the parent eager reference logits (atol=rtol=1e-4, exact top-1) with permanent fallback to the parent path on any breach: (1) fold the 20 eval-mode BatchNorm affines into the preceding FP32 conv weights/biases before capture (algebraically exact refactor in FP32), eliminating the ~42.7 us of per-replay bn_fw_inf kernels and 20 graph nodes; (2) stop re-transforming constant weights per replay where achievable - capture the forward reading directly from the fixed state['pixels'] tensor (identity-guarded, recapture on state change) so the per-run aten::copy_ dispatch and 602 KB device copy disappear, and prefer a capture-time-validated algorithm/layout variant (e.g. NHWC/channels_last for the 115.2 us stem 7x7 stride-2 conv and the ~56 us layer-1 winograd convs) when it is faster and stays within tolerance, since cudnn.benchmark is not touched and the selection is made by explicit try-and-validate at capture, not by changing source policy; (3) keep the fresh logits clone for consumer safety. Expected effect is a reduction from ~0.759 ms toward the ~0.62-0.70 ms range (~43 us BN + ~10-15 us copy/dispatch + 0-90 us conv-selection improvement, individually uncertain), with logits within atol=rtol=1e-4 and identical argmax because every retained computation is algebraically identical or validated against the eager reference. This is a hypothesis to be tested by the framework's independent paired AB/BA measurement; it is rejected if the gain does not exceed the MAD-derived noise bound, if any logit violates tolerance, or if top-1 changes.

proposal.rationale: Repair of the concrete failure recorded in inputs/previous-feedback.txt: the prior selection was an execution_plan over groups 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb + 6870b4a6e1536342a2ef, and its second group (root model-forward, call 80ff8693d7ac3cf2433b10f2) is absent_or_unassociated in the current discovery - the accepted trial-3c7742e65e whole-forward plan replaced run() at project.invoke, so the model-forward boundary and its inner call inventory are no longer observable - so a verbatim resubmission would reference a nonexistent group. This attempt anchors exclusively in the currently eligible groups (routing.selected_groups: 3c57c8731ec33ed76cbb project.invoke, 687b976c828d764c1ab8 aten.copy_, 25f0b0f6ce52aabeb54e aten.clone) and replaces only call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 (project.invoke ABI: callable(state) -> {'logits': ...}). Starting point is the accepted revision at ~0.759 ms (independently measured 0.759316 ms vs 1.531324 reference, quality pass with max_abs_error 0.0), not the 1.630656 ms eager baseline; the 3.846981 ms profiled wall is hook-perturbed and not timing evidence. Diagnostic evidence for the current state (target-resources.json, call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0): 714.341 us CUDA across 81 kernels, all in graph id 2 with root-only association, so the workload is kernel-bound inside the replayed graph with only ~38-45 us of outside-graph wall (copy_ dispatch, graph launch, clone dispatch, sync boundaries). Kernel composition: 347.0 us scudnn winograd 3x3 convs; 228.7 us implicit_convolve_sgemm of which the stem 7x7 stride-2 conv alone is 115.175 us on a pathological 2x16x1 grid of 8x8x1 blocks (2048 threads total); 56.1 us generateWinogradTilesKernel that re-transform the constant FP32 filters every replay; 42.7 us bn_fw_inf over 20 eval-mode BatchNorms; remainder is relu/add/pool/gemm. The candidate is a revised whole-forward capture at the same project.invoke boundary with three mechanisms, each validated once at untimed capture time against the pristine eager reference logits (atol=rtol=1e-4 plus exact argmax) with permanent fallback to the parent on any breach: (1) fold all 20 eval-mode conv->BatchNorm pairs into conv weights/bias (exact FP32 algebra; HF ResNetConvLayer/ResNetShortCut expose the (convolution, normalization) attribute pairs; replaced BN modules are parked under an unused attribute so model.parameters() and the reported parameter_count are unchanged; folding is pre-scanned atomically, idempotent on re-entry, and exactly restorable from weight backups), eliminating the ~42.7 us of per-replay bn_fw_inf kernels and 20 graph nodes; (2) capture the forward reading directly from the fixed state['pixels'] storage (guarded by a data_ptr/shape/stride/dtype token with lazy recapture on change), so the per-run aten::copy_ dispatch and 602 KB device copy disappear entirely - eliminated call 8b4ffbf54af1c1a252b359b6, whose only consumer was the previous plan's own static input buffer, so no external reader is affected, while the fresh aten.clone of the 1x1000 logits (ff665ce97a6a868dae8ae228) is kept for consumer safety; (3) a capture-time-validated memory-format variant: after the NCHW graph is captured and timed, the model is converted to channels_last (weights only; state tensors untouched), eagerly validated, captured and timed, and the faster variant is kept only if it beats NCHW replay by more than 5 us; otherwise the original NCHW parameter storages are restored by identity (p.data = saved) so the kept NCHW graph still aliases the live weights, and the channels_last graph is destroyed. cudnn.benchmark is never touched and TF32 stays disabled; the channels_last choice is an explicit try-and-validate layout selection, not a source-policy change. Expected effect is a reduction from ~0.759 ms toward the ~0.62-0.71 ms range (~43 us BN kernels plus ~5-15 us copy_/dispatch removal are directly attributable; the conv/layout gain of 0-90 us is uncertain and decided by measured replay timing at capture), with logits within atol=rtol=1e-4 and identical argmax because every retained computation is algebraically identical or validated against the pristine eager reference. This bundle writes the same call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0 as the installed trial-3c7742e65e-param-816ab5dc, so it explicitly replaces that whole bundle and preserves its needed behavior (whole-forward CUDA Graph capture/replay with static logits and per-run clone) itself. This is a hypothesis to be tested by the framework's independent paired AB/BA measurement; it is rejected if the gain does not exceed the MAD-derived noise bound, if any logit violates tolerance, or if top-1 changes.

setup_work.build: build(context) performs no CUDA work, no allocations and no parameter transforms; it only closes over the parent reference (references['5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0']) and lazily initialized plan state, and returns the single-call mapping {5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0: _invoke}.
setup_work.first_invocation_untimed: On the first invocation of the installed candidate (framework quality/coverage checks and request warmup=2 precede the timed repeats=5): (a) 3 eager side-stream warm-up forwards of the unchanged model on state['pixels'] plus one logits clone kept as the pristine eager reference; (b) atomic BatchNorm folding - pre-scan of all (convolution, normalization) pairs (20 for ResNet-18), in-place conv.weight scaling, a _FoldedConv2d wrapper carrying the folded bias as a plain (non-Parameter) tensor so parameter_count is unchanged, BN modules parked under an unused attribute and normalization set to Identity, followed by an eager folded-vs-pristine validation (allclose atol=rtol=1e-4 plus argmax equality) with exact unfold-and-disable on failure; (c) whole-forward CUDA graph capture reading state['pixels'] directly (no static input buffer, no per-run copy), one validation replay, and ~40 timed replays via CUDA events; (d) an optional channels_last variant: snapshot of the 4D parameter data tensors, model.to(memory_format=channels_last), 3 side-stream warm-ups, eager validation, capture, validation and ~40 timed replays; the faster variant is kept and the loser destroyed, with NCHW storages restored by identity when channels_last does not win; (e) a final replay revalidation of the winner after any storage restore. The torch.cuda.graph contexts additionally run their standard gc.collect()/torch.cuda.empty_cache() once each at this untimed point. Total untimed setup is well under one second of extra work.
setup_work.steady_state_per_invocation: One cudaGraphLaunch of the captured whole-forward graph (which re-reads the current contents of the state['pixels'] storage each replay) and one 1x1000 FP32 logits clone (4,000 B) outside the graph pool; no aten::copy_ staging dispatch, no caching-allocator activity inside the captured region, and no extra synchronization. Guard checks are a few Python attribute/pointer comparisons.
setup_work.memory_scope: Setup-only transient allocations: BN-fold weight backups and the 4D-parameter snapshot (~47 MB each while alive, freed at the end of setup), the 4 KB eager reference logits, and two whole-forward graph private pools during variant comparison (the loser pool is released when its graph and static logits are dropped). Retained after setup: one CUDA graph private pool holding the captured activation intermediates (same working set the eager forward allocates; exact pool size is not measured here and is left to the framework's counters). framework.peak_allocated_bytes, reset per run, can report a smaller number because allocation moved into the untimed graph capture, while framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes and lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes include capture-time allocation and the retained graph pool increases reserved memory; none of these counters measures non-PyTorch driver allocations. The per-run counter decrease is an accounting effect of moving allocation into capture, not a general physical-memory saving.
setup_work.state_lifecycle: Adapter state is only read (device/model/pixels); reset(state) between repeats is compatible (eval() re-assert and peak-counter reset create no gradients or caches; folding is idempotent under repeated setup). Folding and the channels_last selection mutate invariant model parameters during the first untimed invocation, which is valid for this warm-model inference lifecycle: the returned logits are revalidated against the pristine eager reference at that moment and by the framework's independent checks. The captured graph aliases the live conv-weight storages and the live state['pixels'] storage, so in-place parameter or pixel-content updates through those storages are picked up by replay automatically; if state is re-prepared with a new model object or a different pixels storage (identity-token mismatch), the candidate drops the graph and lazily re-runs the setup pipeline on the fresh state. Inference-mode semantics match adapter._infer; tensors created during setup are only mutated inside inference mode.
setup_work.synchronization: Replay is launched onto the current stream after pure-Python guard checks and completes under the framework's existing synchronize-at-both-boundaries timing; the logits clone is ordered after replay on the same stream. Extra synchronizations happen only during the untimed setup/validation/timing phase.

quality_risks: BatchNorm folding changes floating-point rounding (reassociated scale/shift) even though it is algebraically exact in real arithmetic; it is gated by an eager folded-vs-pristine allclose check at atol=rtol=1e-4 plus argmax equality at untimed capture time, with exact unfold-and-disable on any breach, and the framework's independent logits/top-1 validation remains the binding gate.

The channels_last variant executes different conv kernels with different accumulation order; it is adopted only if both its eager output and its replayed output match the pristine NCHW eager reference at atol=rtol=1e-4 with identical argmax and its measured replay time beats the NCHW graph by more than 5 us; otherwise the original NCHW parameter storages are restored by identity and the variant is discarded, keeping the weights the NCHW graph aliases live.

Model mutations (fold, parked BatchNorm modules, optional channels_last conversion) persist for the process lifetime; if the candidate later fails, the permanent fallback runs the parent path on the mutated model, which was already validated to be within tolerance of the pristine reference at setup time. Weights converted to channels_last inside inference mode cannot be mutated in-place outside inference mode afterwards; this workload performs no such mutations (inference-only, eval mode, no optimizer).

CUDA graph capture can fail on uncommon driver/stream states (default capture_error_mode='global'); any capture, replay, validation or timing exception permanently reverts the invocation path to the parent, so behavior degrades toward baseline rather than below it. Direct-read capture is guarded by a pixels identity token (data_ptr/shape/stride/dtype/device); a changed pixels tensor triggers lazy recapture rather than stale replay, and in-place content changes are picked up automatically because replay re-reads the same storage.

The per-run aten.copy_ staging call (8b4ffbf54af1c1a252b359b6) is eliminated; its only consumer was the previous plan's own static input buffer, which no longer exists, and the new graph reads the live fixture storage each replay, so workload execution on every invocation is preserved and nothing fixture-dependent is cached or precomputed - BN folding is an invariant parameter transform, not an answer cache.

Timing-based variant selection at untimed setup could in principle pick a variant that is not fastest under the framework's wall-clock protocol; the margin (5 us) and 40-replay CUDA-event averaging bound this risk, and both variants are numerically validated before selection.

Memory accounting: per-run peak_allocated_bytes may fall because replay performs no caching-allocator allocations while reserved memory grows by the retained graph pool; setup transients (~47 MB snapshots/backups, second graph pool) are freed before the timed phase. This is reported explicitly and is not claimed as a physical-memory saving.
